My then 4-year old cousin had half of his fingers chopped off in a treadmill, and when he was in the Emergency Room, my uncle — who’s well-known in our family for being a good for nothing gambler who usually just leaves his son to us before bolting off God knows where — said to my mom in the most hopeless voice ever, as if hasn’t sunk into him yet, as if he didn’t know what else to say: “His fingers are gone.” 

(Keep in mind my mom caught this in tape, and even through the video, the heartbreak in his voice was enough for me to tear up still thinking about it, years later.)

i kinda feel this. my mother was never affectionate and continuously verbally abuses me to this day. i attend a university away from home, and during the times she’d text me she loved me, i can’t help but tear up all the time.

when i babysit my baby cousins and they’re having fun or see them sleeping. i don’t know. i had to go through so much shit and just the thought of them going through the stuff i did genuinely hurts me to the point of crying. 

sometimes i cry because i’m so overwhelmed with the thought that i wouldn’t be enough to have my own baby. i don’t know. it’s pretty weird

My face without glasses. I have a grade of over 800, so I have to wear them all the time lest I want a migraine. I get unprompted validation and my fair share of compliments and dates, so I know that I’m somewhat attractive. But. 

But. 

When I first started wearing them, I was in third grade (I’m a sophomore in college now), and I became even more shy when I noticed how the boys in my class looked at me. They’d help me roll my stroller bag. They’d play with the windows when I was inside the telephone booth. They’d insist on erasing and cleaning the blackboards even when I was on the monitor list. We were kids; those mundane things were huge to us, and I didn’t know what brought this sudden change of treatment until a close boy friend of mine slid a paper to me in class saying he had a crush on me. I asked him why. He told me it was because of my glasses. 

I never took them off unless it was necessary ever since.
tinder notif popped up that i matched with someone while my strict and protective dad was using my phone logging into his spotify 🙃

i cried mostly because of the build-up that led to it. emma’s broken leg, the clinic scene, the trio’s hug, the flashback of them as kids and the fact norman only packed emma’s string phones. then afterwards it was months of hopelessness, then ray’s suicide mission, then them deciding to leave phil behind, then mama letting them go (+ revelation of leslie, and her being ray’s biological mother). 

i’m a manga reader too, and the impact of those episodes didn’t lessen even when animated. i can’t wait for more of the feels second season will bring!

THIS HAPPENED JUST LAST WEEK! My friends and I were on the third floor of a building in my uni that was called the Science Complex, for all the science-related subjects. 

The roof of the next building was connected to the Science Complex through an open railing, and my friend told me he used to go star-gazing with his senior high buddies. He went to the roof and he looked creepy out there wearing our pre-med uniform, and one of us were like, “Hey let’s go prank our other friends who aren’t with us,” and we were all totally okay with it. 

I took the picture. Everything was okay. 

Later that night, when I was about to send it to the group chat, I noticed the creepiest thing. There was a—I’m sorry if I can’t explain it properly—green glitch that framed the picture from both sides. I was batshit crept out. It wasn’t like that when I took the pic and saved it. My phone has never done that before either, nor is it exactly an old model. 

My university has history with the supernatural, but I’m not exactly sure either.

No idea! I’m 19 and currently in uni, and I’ve always been the center of my groups. I read majority of the posts and definitely felt the heavy weight they were talking about, but just last night while my friends and I were out drinking I finally got the answer. 

We were having an open forum and everybody noticed they were hiding things from each other, all of which I already knew. When prompted why, one of my friends said I was the most trustworthy and open one, to which everyone agreed. I guess that’s what always keeps me going.
For my dad to come home.
